html:
Martín Fierro is a long poem by the Argentine writer José Hernández, published in two parts in 1872 and 1879. It is regarded as the national poem of Argentina.

Written in the speech of the gauchos, the cowboys of the pampas, it tells of Martín Fierro, a gaucho taken from his family and forced to serve on the frontier against Indigenous raiders. He deserts, finds his home destroyed, kills men in fights and flees to live among the Indigenous people. The poem protested at how the state treated the gauchos, whom men like Sarmiento saw as barbarians.

It was hugely popular among country people, who memorised it. By the time the gaucho way of life of the pulperías had faded, the poem made the gaucho the symbol of Argentina. Borges wrote about it and its hero.
sum: Martín Fierro is a long poem by the Argentine writer José Hernández, published in two parts in 1872 and 1879. It is regarded as the national poem of Argentina.
